(1) MinRev pricing is stable for networks with single- power-law congestion costs, and (2) the BPR cost function has a single-power law congestion cost, and therefore, MinRev tolls for BPR cost functions are stable.

the MinRev toll is stable (flow independent) if and only if the congestion cost function has a single power-law congestion term, and that the MinRev flow is nearly equal to the SO flow, if the demand is relatively insensitive.

the BPR cost function is sufficient for stability of MinRev tolling in networks, that MinRev tolling is flow-independent in the case of all links in use, and that MinRev tolls can approximate MC tolls in the case of major congestion and inelastic demand.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MinRev tolls have the potential to be a good second-best solution, in situations where MC tolls are not feasible.
MinRev tolls have a strong claim to be the most desirable tolling policy for transportation networks, and should be considered as an important alternative to MC pricing.
MinRev tolls can provide a good approximation of the economic efficiency of MC tolls, and are more stable and less complex, and thus more desirable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MinRev toll is the best toll that can be used to achieve the most economic efficiency of network traffic, while still maintaining a fixed toll.
MinRev tolls, while not as efficient as MC tolls, may be quite acceptable in practice, especially if there is a need to stabilize toll revenues.

the stability of MinRev tolling in transportation networks is guaranteed for a single power-law congestion function (such as the BPR function), and is also guaranteed for any network with a single bottleneck.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BPR cost function is a sufficient (but not necessary) condition for the stability of Minimal Revenue tolls in transportation network.

the BPR cost function, which is the most widely used cost function in transportation networks, has an important property: its minimal-revenue tolls are stable, i.e., the tolls do not change with flow, for a wide class of networks.
MinRev pricing can provide a good compromise between the economic benefits of MC pricing and the practical benefits of fixed tolls.
